Furthermore, while indexes for keyword search are quite efficient, here we provide insights into how to improve the scalability of prefiltering techniques for semantic search, comparing LSH indexes with Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds. Our experiments show that HNSW drastically improves the runtime of semantic table search by 4.7X on average whilst retaining the high-quality tables. Abstract:Long user behavior sequences are among the strongest signals for click-through rate (CTR) prediction. At each layer, the request representation (the search query, user features and scene) first reads the sequence. Each behavior token then attends to the updated request representation and uses what it reads to update itself, so the next layer reads a sequence shaped by the current request. Abstract:Text-based generative recommenders can go beyond ranking existing items by directly generating item titles or other textual representations. Abstract:A recommendation page is consumed as a whole: the items on it compete for attention and complement one another, so the best page is not simply the individually best items placed side by side. We study whole-page optimization, which selects and orders the items on a page jointly to maximize the score of the page. The number of possible pages grows combinatorially, so good pages must be generated rather than enumerated. Some generative re-ranking methods use the same page-level training signal for every choice in a sampled page. Others imitate target pages built before training, which remain largely fixed as the generator improves. We address both limitations with one local page-level objective, which repeatedly moves the current generator toward pages with higher score. This objective splits exactly into one training target per position, and each target compares candidates at the same partial page by the scores of the complete pages they lead to. Every position therefore learns to choose the item that is better for the whole page, rather than the item that looks best on its own. We call this procedure whole-page policy improvement. On two public datasets, KuaiRand-1K and RL4RS-SeqSlate, which cover multi-objective item selection and constrained ordering, and on an industrial dataset of logged pages, our method outperforms the evaluated generative re-ranking baselines. Abstract:Generative retrieval (GR) for sequential recommendation compresses each item into a short semantic ID and trains an autoregressive decoder to generate next-item codes from a user history. While appealing for cold-start handling and storage, au- toregressive GR suffers a structural scaling limit: typically, longer semantic IDs reduce quantization error in principle but degrade ranking quality and quadratic memory usage against semantic ID length. We propose Late Quantization (LQ), a non-autoregressive paradigm that confines discretization to the output (item) side of the pipeline. The encoder and scoring rule operate in continuous space, while items are stored and matched as semantic IDs produced by an end-to-end-trained residual quantizer. This architectural shift permits an additive error decomposition and a pairwise ordering theorem that jointly bound the quantization- induced ranking drop, a structural guarantee absent in prior semantic-ID recommenders. Across four public benchmarks, the resulting recommender, LQ-Rec, delivers three capabilities simultaneously: ranking quality improves monotonically with the semantic-ID length and outperforms existing baselines; a single trained model supports anytime compression, tuning ranking quality against inference cost without retraining; and LQ-Rec shows superior generalization on a memorization/generalization partition.

Abstract:Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in open-domain question answering, but often struggle with factual accuracy and multi-hop reasoning due to the incompleteness of the training corpora. Rather than assuming manually defined semantic roles, these latent perspectives are adaptively aggregated to capture heterogeneous relevance signals during retrieval. Abstract:Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is currently revolutionizing content creation across various media. Yet interaction with these systems often relies on discrete, turn-based prompting that can interrupt flow and constrain expression to symbolic text. We explore physiological signals as a source of continuous adaptation without explicit commands, as a path toward embodied co-creation. This paper presents ReTiNA-Cinema, a methodological proof-of-concept that integrates electroencephalography (EEG) with generative AI to enable physiologically guided visual modulation of cinematic material. By linking physiological activity to the evolving appearance of a film, the system provides a basis for exploring embodied sense-making, in which viewers’ bodily responses contribute to shaping the sensory experience through which they interpret the unfolding scenes. The system combines real-time EEG signal processing with a generative AI pipeline based on Stable Diffusion Turbo for frame-level image transformation. Single-user and two-user configurations map EEG-derived features to prompt selection and transformation strength. Abstract:Differential privacy (DP) is increasingly adopted to protect sensitive data in visualization, but understanding how privacy-induced noise affects visual representations remains fragmented. Prior work has examined the impact of DP noise on specific chart types, yet these findings are typically tied to particular chart types and evaluation settings, making it difficult to generalize across contexts. In parallel, visualization research has long established that visual channels, the visual properties of marks that encode data attributes, differ in perceptual effectiveness under noise-free conditions. However, these principles have not been systematically revisited under DP, where noise is deliberately introduced into the data to protect privacy. In this paper, we present a channel-centric perspective to reframe prior empirical and theoretical results. Our synthesis drawson prior findings to motivate a channel-read-mechanism hypothesis: the utility of DP visualizations may depend on the task-relevant reads made salient by visual channel configurations and DP mechanism choice jointly. Moreover, this perspective highlights the role of channel choice throughout the privacy-preserving visualization pipeline, from disclosure framing and DP algorithm design to utility evaluation and interpretation of noisy outputs. The synthesis also identifies gaps in the existing evaluation literature and highlights research opportunities for channel-aware DP visualization.

Abstract:Social virtual reality (VR) platforms have surged in popularity but continue to face significant security challenges, including privacy invasion and user manipulation. Yet, the security risks posed by deceptive content remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce four novel deceptive UI attacks that covertly manipulate social VR users into performing unintended actions without their awareness. We show how adversarial content creators can embed seemingly benign scripts and interactive elements within carefully designed virtual worlds, deceiving users into unknowingly carrying out harmful behaviors. We implemented these attacks on VRChat, a leading social VR platform, and an IRB-approved user study involving 30 participants confirmed their effectiveness. To mitigate these threats, we propose MetaScanner, a proactive analysis system that efficiently scans virtual world assets, including scripts and interactive objects, to identify suspicious or deceptive elements before users are exposed to them. We demonstrate that MetaScanner can successfully detect all threats in test worlds where the four attack scenarios were implemented. Additionally, MetaScanner shows its lightweight nature, with an average scanning time of 5 seconds across 38 real-world assets.

[HC-8] Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25577
作者: Ishita Asnani,Shaghayegh Fazliani,Zachary Ryan,Kriyoshig Prasai,Chirag Kumar,Indra Gonzalez Ojeda,Marc Lipsitch,Madeleine Udell
类目: Machine Learning (cs.LG); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Objective: Case investigation and contact tracing are labor-intensive. Web forms struggle when respondents need clarification before disclosing contacts, and open-ended chatbots may deviate from protocols. We developed and evaluated Epira, a protocol-controlled large language model (LLM) interviewer for multi-disease case investigation and contact tracing. Materials and Methods: Epira pairs LLM dialogue with a rule-based controller enforcing required questions, safety handoffs, and a structured case record, and adapts to new diseases by questionnaire upload. Local (Qwen2.5) and cloud (GPT-5.4) backends were tested. Study 1 used 108 simulated cases with ground-truth fields and contacts for measles and gonorrhea under Epira and open-ended conditions (864 sessions). Study 2 enrolled 72 volunteers in a 2 \times 2 disease-by-model interview assessing completion, usability, acceptability, and trust. Results: Across Study 1, Epira with a local LLM captured 88.9% of required fields and 60.1% of ground-truth contacts. Open-ended interviewers recovered 31.1-41.9 percentage points fewer required fields than the same models in Epira. In Study 2, completion was 100%; mean adapted System Usability Scale (SUS) was 82.95 \pm 16.17 on a 0-100 scale and mean trust was 3.85 \pm 0.77 on a 1-5 scale. Discussion: Protocol control drove completeness more than model choice. Local and cloud deployments produced similar records, supporting privacy-preserving local use with human review of routed interviews and missed contacts. Conclusion: Epira recovers required fields and contacts under diverse disclosure conditions, works with local and cloud LLMs, and received favorable usability and trust ratings. [HC-9] Persona Lenses: What Makes a Vision-Language Model See Through Its Personas Eyes?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25508
作者: Yoonho Shin
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注: 29 pages, 9 figures, 14 tables, including supplementary material

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Vision-language models have been used to simulate where a user looks on a web page. However, a persona in the prompt reaches the simulated gaze only partly. We measure this reach as the difference in one model’s gaze between two MatrAIx personas that differ in a single attribute. We introduce persona lenses, which place the persona between the model and the page: a text lens (a two-step prompt in which the model first writes what the persona would look at), a pixel lens (marks on the region matching the persona’s interests) and a weight lens (a dwell reward gated to keep the scanpath natural). Using Qwen3-VL (4B and 32B) and Qwen3.5-9B on generated and live pages, we compare the lenses with one another and with scale, the 32B model with no lens. It has been confirmed that the text lens separates the personas strongly but is not robust to profile changes that should not move gaze. The pixel lens separates the personas less but is unaffected by attributes unrelated to gaze. At 4B and 9B, the weight lens separates the personas on interests held out from training, with no extra step on a new page. The 32B model separates the personas with the base prompt alone. Therefore, the choice of a lens depends on cost and model size.

[HC-10] GenAI-DBT: Evaluating a DBT-Informed Generative AI Platform for Mindfulness Skills Training: A Pilot Randomized Study

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25428
作者: Jingchen Ye(1),Yujia Chen(2),Leyang Han(1),Siyuan Wang(3),Mark Zachary Rosenthal(4 and 5),Yucheng Jin(1) ((1) Division of Natural and Applied Sciences, Duke Kunshan University, (2) Department of Applied Psychology, School of Social and Behavioral Sciences, Nanjing University, (3) Department of Psychological Sciences, College of William and Mary, (4) Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, Duke University Medical Center, (5) Department of Psychology and Neuroscience, Duke University)

Abstract:We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and engagement of three digital formats for dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) mindfulness skills training. In a 30-day randomized pilot study, 45 university students were assigned to GenAI-DBT, a general-purpose large language model chatbot (Chatbot), or a static web resource (Web). Forty-two completed the study, and nine completed follow-up interviews. Usability scores were within acceptable ranges across conditions, with no significant between-group differences. GenAI-DBT showed the highest observed participant-week adherence (71.4%, vs. 53.3% for Web and 42.3% for Chatbot), a descriptive difference. Mindful Attention Awareness Scale and Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale scores showed no significant time-by-group interactions, and session-level self-reported mood changes did not differ significantly across conditions. GenAI-DBT showed a larger positive change in linguistic valence than Chatbot (4.28 vs. 1.59, P = .02, Cohen’s d = 0.99). Interviewees valued contextualized, scenario-based practice and identified response latency, repetition, and limited personalization as areas for improvement. The findings support the feasibility and acceptability of DBT-informed conversational AI for skills practice and motivate further evaluation in larger, more clinically relevant samples. Clinical efficacy remains to be established.

[HC-11] When Should Deployed BCI Decoders Adapt? A Resource-Priced Ladder for Frozen EEG Trunks

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25315
作者: Sergey Musienko
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Neurons and Cognition (q-bio.NC)
备注: 16 pages, 7 tables, 5 figures, 1 appendix. Companion paper: arXiv:2607.22397 . Code: pip install nimbus-bci (v0.9.0)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:When should a deployed MI decoder spend adaptation resources-not only how to adapt under shift? We study a thin control layer outside a frozen encoder: a resource ladder (factory - Bayesian head - affine map, with full fine-tune as an escape hatch) governed by regime-aware gating under a utility that prices accuracy, fit time, and label cost. The head is Bayesian in the conjugate sense: a Normal-Inverse-Wishart prior over the class conditional Gaussians in embedding space, updated in closed form (no gradients) as labelled trials arrive. Full estimators, constants, and the reanalysis code are in the companion paper and the ancillary bundle of this submission. Thesis: adaptation should be gated and capped, not always-on and not blindly fine-tuned. Evidence: (i) utility-max gating over-adapts on clean data that already carries session drift; a clean-referenced gate restores low false-entry rates (e.g. dropping the adaptation rate from 0.56 to 0.11 on field-like sessions, with the cascade staying on the factory decoder for ~87% of clean cells). (ii) Under severe synthetic stress, a lightweight LDA head matches or exceeds the frozen trunk’s accuracy across five encoder architectures (n=155 subject x trunk cells, pooled across shared subjects), at ~23x lower fit time than full warm-start fine-tuning. Always-on baselines favor capping the default below full fine-tune. (iii) In two no-perturbation BNCI session checks the factory model transferred without intervention (no reliable head gain), so the control layer’s value under natural drift is cost-efficiency and clean-safety rather than demonstrated accuracy gains. (iv) Adaptation severity does not follow a universal ordinal ladder across datasets, highlighting the need for dynamic gating over fixed adaptation policies.

[HC-12] Modeling Learner-Technology Interaction Through Multilevel Gaze Transition Dynamics to Inform Usability in Online Learning

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25294
作者: Yueqi Weng,Jie “Jennifer” Lu,fan Yang
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Gaze data provide fine-grained evidence of how learners engage with instructional content and interface elements, complementing conventional usability evaluation methods. However, eye-tracking analyses often examine within-slide visual attention and across-slide navigation separately, limiting understanding of learner interaction throughout extended learning experiences. This exploratory multi-method study integrated area-of-interest transitions, gaze entropy, slide-level navigation, and network-based representations to analyze seven eye-tracking recordings of high school students interacting with an AI-supported online biology lesson, complemented by three post-intervention focus groups. Results showed individual differences in within-slide gaze allocation and switching patterns. Learners followed shared navigation pathways but differed in revisiting and immediate return behaviors. The focus group findings highlighted positive perceptions of interactive materials and AI-generated feedback, alongside usability concerns related to navigation, interface clarity, and assessment guidance. Together, these outcomes show how integrating multilevel gaze analytics with learner perspectives can provide complementary evidence for identifying interaction trends relevant to usability evaluation. Future research should test this approach with larger, more diverse samples and examine relationships among gaze patterns, usability, and learning outcomes.

[HC-13] AI-Induced Social Erosion: Using LLM s for Work Tasks Reduces Help-Seeking Intentions Towards Colleagues

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25269
作者: Kevin Chow,Sophia Deng,Bowen He,Hanyi Min,Qiaosi Wang,Koustuv Saha,Vedant Das Swain
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC); Computers and Society (cs.CY)
备注: 36 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables, preprint

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Generative AI is becoming embedded in knowledge work as an intelligent collaborator to assist in completing tasks. However, this readily available assistance risks displacing key interactions through which colleague relationships are built and sustained at work. This paper leverages the concept of help-seeking behaviour to investigate whether and how AI usage shapes colleague relationships. We conducted an online experimental vignette study where 248 knowledge workers evaluated scenarios that systematically varied whether and how AI was used across different work tasks. Using linear mixed-effects models, we found that AI-enabled work reduced help-seeking intentions compared to non-AI work across tasks, and especially for brainstorming. Visible AI usage was associated with greater help-seeking intentions towards colleagues, and individual contributors’ colleague relationships were more vulnerable than managers. Our findings identify opportunities for workplace AI tools, practices, and policies to preserve colleague relationships in increasingly AI-integrated workplaces.

[HC-14] AI Deactivation Reduces Loneliness and Increases Social Interaction

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25263
作者: Dora Zhao,Grace Wang,Yutong Zhang,Lujain Ibrahim,Robert E. Kraut,Diyi Yang
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC); Computers and Society (cs.CY)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:General-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) assistants are increasingly embedded in everyday life, transforming how people accomplish tasks and potentially reshaping how they interact with others. Prior research has focused on how using AI for explicitly social purposes affects users’ psychological well-being and social lives. Yet such uses account for only a small portion of interactions with general-purpose AI assistants. Whether using AI for everyday, instrumental tasks affects users’ psychological well-being and social behavior remains unclear. Here we investigate these effects through a longitudinal deactivation experiment with active ChatGPT users (N=625), in which participants were randomly assigned to abstain from using AI assistants for either fourteen days (treatment) or one day (control). Participants used AI predominantly for instrumental purposes, with 84.7% reporting productivity as their most frequent use case. Two weeks of deactivation significantly reduced loneliness relative to the control group ( \beta = -0.10 , p=0.03 ), with reductions persisting two weeks after participants resumed using AI ( \beta = -0.16 , p=0.02 ). Deactivation also significantly increased the number of people participants interacted with in person and the time they spent socializing over the intervention period. Open-ended responses indicate that during the deactivation period participants sought help from others for tasks they otherwise would have delegated to AI and redirected attention toward social interaction. Overall, our findings suggest that even when AI is used primarily to accomplish instrumental tasks, it may inadvertently reduce opportunities for social interaction and connection.

[HC-15] Design and Evaluation of a Body-Machine Interface as an Alternative Control Paradigm for Pedal-based Sewing Machines

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25261
作者: Ashrut Aryal,Rajiv Ranganathan,Ranjan Mukherjee
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Body-machine interfaces (BoMIs) exploit body movements to control assistive devices; they have been evaluated primarily in tasks such as cursor control or robotic manipulation where the entire movement repertoire is devoted toward device control. However, tasks with multiple concurrent processes require the user to share the movement repertoire used for device control with other body movements for task execution. This issue is examined here in the context of sewing, where the sewing machine is typically controlled by a pedal in coordination with hand movements for guiding the fabric. We evaluated the learning of a trunk-controlled BoMI for sewing machine control, and compared it with conventional pedal control. Twenty-four novice participants (12 BoMI, 12 Pedal) completed 10 trials of a standardized sewing assessment followed by 3 trials of a transfer task. The BoMI mapped trunk movements to the sewing machine’s full functional repertoire, which included continuous speed control of the needle, and discrete actions such as presser-foot and needle lifts. The two groups learned at comparable rates, showing similar completion times and error counts; for both groups, completion time reduced by approximately 30%. Additional analyses showed that the BoMI group had fewer presser-foot lift errors during training and fewer errors on the first transfer trial. Both groups also exhibited similar subjective workload. These findings collectively demonstrate that a BoMI interface can support sewing-machine control during concurrent manual activity, highlighting the potential for using BoMIs for increasing accessibility in industrial workplace contexts.

[HC-16] owards Restorative Urban Spaces: An Exploratory Field Study of Nature Videos on Public Multi-Display Signage

作者: Yuri Mikawa,Takumi Yokosaka,Yuki Kubota,Kazushi Maruya
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:In recent years, multi-display signage (MDS) has become increasingly common in urban stations, plazas, and other public spaces, where it is primarily used to present advertisements and information. Beyond these conventional applications, MDS offers opportunities to shape people’s experiences of public environments through spatially distributed and dynamic visual content. Motivated by the potential of mediated nature to support restorative experiences in urban environments, we conducted a nine-day exploratory field study in a free-admission area of a science museum, presenting artificial intelligence (AI)-generated nature videos across four displays and collecting 1,263 questionnaire responses. We combined three complementary analyses. First, structural equation modeling identified strong associations among perceived consistency across displays, presence, and self-reported restorative responses, consistent with our theoretically motivated model. Second, exploratory comparisons across video-presentation configurations revealed modest differences in consistency and restoration ratings, although these AI-generated videos did not significantly outperform the advertisement reference. Third, qualitative analysis of open-ended responses identified fascination, immersion, and restorative feelings, alongside concerns about naturalness, visual quality, and motion-related discomfort. Together, these findings provide empirical insights into MDS-mediated nature experiences, with implications for nature-video design and questionnaire refinement. They also inform a tentative conceptual extension of the model incorporating additional perceptual and evaluative factors.

[HC-17] Crisis Governance at the Joints. Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies: The Case of Human-Swarm Teaming

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25202
作者: Anthony Longo
类目: Computers and Society (cs.CY); Emerging Technologies (cs.ET); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC); Robotics (cs.RO)
备注: 3 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. It unpacks this territory with a 3i-framework, the Interface, where operators and swarms work together, the Infrastructure, where organisations distribute tasks, decisions and blame, and the Imaginary, where law, policy and shared societal assumptions define what a crisis is and which interventions it justifies. The central claim is that these concerns cannot be addressed one level at a time. Many of the most pressing problems, such as responsibility gaps and the erosion of meaningful human control, arise at the joints between levels, through four translations, habits harden, routines become stories, principles become procedures, and procedures become prompts. Drawing on a critical review of literature across philosophy of technology, political theory, moral psychology, philosophy of mind, AI ethics, and critical disaster and security studies, the report develops this framework, illustrates it with two worked examples, and derives design and governance implications and a set of questions for developers, emergency organisations and policymakers.

[HC-18] Squoosh Bench: Evaluating UX-1 on 318 Historical Website A/B Tests

Abstract:Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. Page roles were masked and recorded outcomes were withheld during inference. Squoosh UX-1, a model fine-tuned on human browsing data, simulated 1,000 shoppers per arm and correctly classified 267 of 318 outcomes (84.0%, 95% Wilson interval 79.5-87.6%, treating experiments as independent). Qwen3 Next 80B, the strongest general-purpose configuration on outcome accuracy, correctly classified 196 of 318 (61.6%). UX-1 favored the variant in 126 experiments. In the live tests, 118 of those variants won (93.7%), four lost, and four had inconclusive results. The remaining 192 experiments included 19 additional variant wins.

[HC-19] Open Response Explorer: a Structured Collaborative Writing System for Peer-Informed Open-Response Assignments

Abstract:Peer-informed open-response assignments (where students view, connect, and learn from peer contributions) hold the potential to foster collaborative knowledge building, yet the unstructured nature of free-form prose prevents students from effectively comparing and making sense of peers’ work. We present Open Response Explorer, an interface that recenters open responses on structured idea units through purpose-based writing and peer response exploration, augmented by common-role text segment highlighting for easy comparison. A within-subjects lab study (N=12) validated the usefulness and usability of the system, demonstrating how it shaped the open-response drafting and peer exploration practices. We discuss implications for purpose-centered authoring and exploration that transform free-form prose into structured, comparable, and collectively navigable knowledge artifacts.

[HC-20] CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25109
作者: Shwetanshu Singh,Mark Keavney,Mathieu Duteil,Meriem Mehri,Scott Blain
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注: 25 pages, 7 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users’ parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users’ gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. We report results for eight frontier models from four providers and observe that under our primary judge, multi-turn escalation raises parasocial behavior on the anthropomorphism and the attachment composite scores across all models. Six of the eight models show a significant increase in overall parasocial reinforcement over control when all three dimensions are escalated simultaneously. We find that within-provider differences are small relative to cross-provider differences, which suggests that provider-level choices such as post-training, rather than model scale, shape parasocial reinforcement and that provider-side intervention may be feasible.

[HC-21] A Human-Centric Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Digital Twin Framework for Cyber-Physical Systems

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25082
作者: Clarisa Grijalva-Lugo,Yu-Zheng Lin,Shalaka Satam,Sicong Shao,Jesus Pacheco,Soheil Salehi,Pratik Satam
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC); Systems and Control (eess.SY)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Digital twins of cyber-physical systems must operate with scarce data, on assets that change after deployment, and for humans whose needs differ, yet existing implementations fix fidelity at design time and do not match the representation to the human or the task. This paper proposes a human-centric adaptive multi-fidelity digital twin framework that models the evolving human, the physical twin, and the digital twin core, and adds a human inference and adaptation function that estimates the human state, predicts the response, and adapts the representation. The framework defines low-, medium-, and high-fidelity tiers distinguished by adaptivity and by coupling, quantified as the ratio of the digital twin latency to the duration of the process step it follows. Three proof-of-concept instantiations are evaluated: a virtual reality tutor, a computer numerical control milling model, and an industrial training station. The low tier estimated learner sentiment with an accuracy of 0.86. The forecasters of the milling model and the training station, both medium-tier, showed a normalized error decline of 0.39 to 0.89 and a human adaptation gain of 1.16 to 1.51, but their latency exceeded the physical process step by 25 to 87 times. Only the station’s vision model met the physical step. The tiers are separated by which functions adapt and where the latency constraint lies, not by a monotone increase in gain or coupling.

[CV-0] Posterior Matching Distillation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26629
作者: Hidir Yesiltepe,Julius Berner,Arash Vahdat,Pinar Yanardag
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Project Page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher’s iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student’s output distribution to the teacher’s. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher’s full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

[CV-1] RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26627
作者: Tuna Han Salih Meral,Kaan Oktay,Alec Helbling,Atakan Kara,Duen Horng Chau,Pinar Yanardag
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注: Project page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

[CV-2] PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26624
作者: Weihao Cheng
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. Abstract:Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O ^2 LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Abstract:Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. Abstract:Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Abstract:Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. Abstract:Reliable extraction of calcium-dependent fluorescence traces in calcium imaging sequences requires identifying pixels whose fluorescence intensity reflects the same underlying cellular activity. Abstract:Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. This latent-free design removes the reconstruction bottleneck, brings training under an objective in the native voxel domain, and yields meshes with substantially richer local detail. The predicted camera and native SDF voxel output further make Direct3D-V3 extensible to generative reconstruction, where diffusion is interleaved with normal-guided refinement to improve alignment with the observed view while the generative prior completes unseen regions. Abstract:Commercial video-generation APIs bill by model and tier, while intermediaries could substitute cheaper models, lower tiers, or cached clips. Abstract:Feed-forward models have been very successful in 3D reconstruction with ad hoc attention designs that relate all view patches densely. However, the cost of this dense global attention grows quadratically with the number of views, preventing the model from applying to larger-scale reconstruction settings. In this paper, we argue that most dense attention computations are unnecessary from a classical structure-from-motion perspective: 3D structures stem from geometrically matching regions in 2D. We bring this principle to learning-based feed-forward reconstruction with our Sparse Geometric Attention Reconstruction (SGAR) method. In SGAR, each patch token attends to only a small set of patch tokens from other views, chosen by a lightweight learned key selection module trained to predict cross-view 3D proximity of tokens. Thus, dense global attention is replaced by much more efficient geometric-similarity-guided sparse attention. SGAR is a general method that can be applied to different feed-forward models by fine-tuning. In our experiments, we show that SGAR is the fastest among both state-of-the-art dense and sparse methods and the most accurate sparse one. It runs up to 12-times faster than dense attention at 1,000 views with stable pose accuracy where existing sparse methods fail, and shows the best performance in reconstructing more complete geometries on the same time budget.

Abstract:Proactive video assistants must decide not only what to say, but also when to speak. Abstract:Recent advances in image restoration have greatly improved global image fidelity, producing visually plausible results across most regions of an image. Nevertheless, even high-quality restorations often exhibit localized failures, including artifacts in semantically important regions such as faces and text, structural inconsistencies, and texture mismatches. Although these errors typically affect only a small portion of the image, they often dominate the overall perceptual quality of the result. In this work, we propose Failure-Aware Image Restoration (FAIR) to address the “last-mile” problem in image restoration. Rather than applying one uniform generative prior over the whole image, we condition a single-pass restoration model on both where local failures are likely to occur and what corrective guidance each region requires. This region-bound conditioning enables fine-grained and controllable restoration that improves semantic accuracy and stylistic consistency in critical regions while maintaining faithful, high-quality restoration elsewhere. Our method complements existing restoration pipelines by shifting the emphasis from global fidelity to local perceptual acceptability. Extensive experiments show that the proposed approach resolves common failure cases and improves perceptual quality, bridging the gap between technical accuracy and practical usability.

Abstract:Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

Abstract:Retrieval-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) models enable efficient test-time adaptation by leveraging expert demonstrations as additional context without updating model parameters. Specifically, R2-VLA learns an uncertainty predictor that estimates the uncertainty of the VLA’s predicted actions given the retrieved demonstrations, guiding when to act autonomously or request expert assistance. We further introduce a task-level risk-control procedure that calibrates the uncertainty threshold to satisfy a user-specified task-failure risk requirement. Moreover, R2-VLA continually incorporates expert corrections into its retrieval memory to improve future adaptation while preserving the prescribed task-level risk guarantee. Abstract:First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network’s weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator’s next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: this https URL.

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26433
作者: Hrishikesh Viswanath,Aniket Bera
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Understanding how objects move in dynamic scenes requires recovering their 3D motion from visual observations and predicting their positions at unobserved times. Existing methods either optimize scene-specific velocity fields or impose predefined physical and kinematic assumptions. We instead study learning a continuous-time dynamics operator across scenes, mapping multi-view visual observations to 3D object kinematics. We introduce Adaptive Pixel Flows (\ours), which learns this operator from multi-view RGB-D observations without per-scene optimization or predefined motion models. The method fuses observations from all cameras into a shared voxel grid in world coordinates, from which the network predicts a continuous-time velocity field. Because the operator is trained across scenes, it learns motion priors that carry over to unseen scenes. The field can then be integrated from observed states to predict object positions between observations and beyond the observed sequence. On held-out PhysInOne scenes, \ours improves F1 over the strongest competing method by 2.5% for in-between prediction and 15% for future prediction. Compared with per-scene velocity-field methods, the improvements are 30% and 85%, respectively. Applied zero-shot to Spring-Gaus, it improves future-prediction F1 by 12%.

Abstract:Immersive 3D content allows text and graphical elements, such as subtitles, annotations, and icons, to be placed inside a scene rather than displayed as flat overlays. Placed this way, they respect occlusion and perspective and take on user-assigned materials and lighting while preserving their original shapes. In Gaussian scenes, however, each new glyph or icon requires its own iterative optimization, which limits scalable content creation. We present FFGaussType, which converts extruded glyph and SVG outlines into Gaussian assets in a single forward pass. A point encoder maps anchors sampled on the known surface to a single feature plane, from which a decoder shared by all assets predicts neural Gaussians carrying surface normals. This separates geometric conversion from material and lighting choices, and the feature plane supports image and video coding for compact delivery. We construct a paired dataset of 27,221 glyph and SVG icon assets with anchors and calibrated normal and silhouette renderings, holding out font families for evaluation. Conversion from prepared anchors takes 9.1 ms per asset, at a fraction of the compute and memory of prior baselines. On unseen font families and test icons, FFGaussType achieves 1.62^\circ normal error and 0.985 silhouette IoU, the best among the compared feed-forward converters, matching the fidelity that per-asset fitting needs thousands of steps to reach. The code and dataset will be released after publication.

Abstract:A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and \pi_0.5 in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.

Abstract:Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbfWeMM-Video, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL. Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks. Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeMM-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.

Abstract:It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks on Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS and Entity-30. We report more than 2,600 such edit processes, whereby each edit is scored on held-out images for success, side effects and accuracy loss. Abstract:Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

Abstract:Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model’s own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: this https URL.

Abstract:At large events, pedestrian tracking supports entrance and passageway counts, but totals hide which crossings were missed. In a stadium study, the system recorded about four in five clearly visible crossings but fewer than one in three mostly obscured crossings. The videos lacked trajectories annotated across frames, so we turned to MOT20, which provides pedestrian trajectories and visibility. We introduce GateTrace to locate missed crossings and assess changes to counting rules. It derives reference crossings from annotations under fixed rules, matches reports by person, direction, time and position, and traces misses through saved boxes and counting decisions. With a shared detector, ByteTrack, OC-SORT and BoT-SORT recover 38.9-46.7% of low-visibility reference crossings on development sequences, versus 98.1-99.0% at high visibility. The gap recurs on two further sequences under a protocol fixed in advance. Published outputs of MOT20-tuned BASE recover 63-78% at low visibility across both sequence groups. Losses stop at different stages across systems. Across four systems and both groups, 47-79% of low-visibility misses have no nearby output linked to the person or no possible crossing in the saved tracks. Removing later checks from BASE on development sequences leaves most misses unresolved and lowers precision against the fixed reference list from about 96% to 77%. Misses also remain among sampled reference crossings that two human annotators supported after checking the videos. GateTrace shows where crossings are lost and measures the recovery and precision costs of changing later checks. We will release the code and per-crossing records.

Abstract:External-eye photography captures clinically relevant periocular anatomy at low acquisition cost, yet no large-scale standardized resource exists for evaluating self-supervised external-eye representations. We introduce a 4.35-million-image Standardized External-Eye Corpus (SEEC) derived from fourteen heterogeneous public face datasets, together with a benchmark for external-eye representation learning. For evaluation, we provide held-out evaluation distributions, landmark-annotated anatomical probe sets, and clinical disease-classification experiments spanning ptosis, thyroid eye disease, and craniofacial syndromes. We evaluate representations at two complementary levels: (a) the representation level, by assessing embedding geometry across multiple data distributions, and (b) the functional level, by assessing anatomical recovery, out-of-distribution anatomical transfer, and disease classification. Our models include ResNet-101 and ViT-B encoders pretrained using InfoNCE, VICReg, and LeJEPA objectives and compared with DINOv2 and MAE. Our results indicate that representation-level and functional-level evaluations are dissociable: broader embedding-space utilization does not consistently correspond to anatomical transfer or disease-classification performance, and no single encoder is universally optimal. Domain-specific external-eye encoders outperform DINOv2 and MAE on cross-dataset anatomical transfer despite being pretrained at substantially smaller scale, while external-eye-pretrained ViT models match or outperform these general-purpose baselines on frozen disease-classification probes. Abstract:Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer’s motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer’s overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric video sources. Complementary rewards assess factual accuracy and coverage, measure step-level temporal alignment, and penalize fragmented or redundant narration, guiding caption refinement through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To improve the reliability of factual supervision, we supplement caption references with pose-derived motion facts when sensor data are available. Across five egocentric benchmarks, EgoCaptioner achieves leading performance among evaluated open-source models in caption quality, caption-conditioned question answering, and temporal alignment. It also surpasses Gemini 3.1 Pro on PhysCapBench and all evaluated proprietary baselines on Minerva-Ego under the caption-to-QA protocol. Ablations support the complementary roles of factual and temporal rewards and show that coarse-to-fine annotation provides more effective supervision than single-pass annotation.

Abstract:Low-dose and thin-slice computed tomography (CT) images suffer from elevated noise that obscures anatomical detail, while clean references for supervised denoising are often unavailable. Although Noise2Noise permits self-supervised training from noisy pairs, direct regression tends to oversmooth fine structure. Averaging multiple independently generated samples mitigates this blur, though repeating multi-step diffusion sampling is costly. We introduce Noise2Noise with Improved Mean Flow (N2N-iMF) to accelerate this process via few-step sampling. N2N-iMF learns to generate one noisy image conditioned on its paired counterpart; at inference, independent outputs are sampled and averaged to suppress noise. We evaluated image quality and sampling efficiency on simulated thin-slice brain and low-dose abdominal CT across four sampling methods and averaging counts from 1 to 20, and validated the approach on real-world photon-counting CT (PCCT) brain scans. With ten samples per conditioning input and three network evaluations per sample, N2N-iMF achieved a mean absolute error of 2.60 HU on brain CT and 14.02 HU on abdominal CT, outperforming 50-evaluation denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) sampling (2.91 and 14.53 HU). On the same GPU, per-output generation time dropped from 7.29 to 0.43 s. Across eight PCCT cases, N2N-iMF reached a mean gray-white matter contrast-to-noise ratio of 1.341, versus 0.916 for Noise2Noise and 1.176 for DDIM. N2N-iMF accelerates self-supervised generative CT denoising without distillation while keeping the number of averaged outputs adjustable at inference.

Abstract:Monitoring physiological parameters such as respiratory rate ( f_R ) is essential for diagnosing and managing various pathological conditions. Thermal imaging offers a promising contactless alternative to traditional methods, which often rely on partially invasive sensors or obtrusive wearable systems. However, existing approaches for f_R estimation from thermal signals typically require extensive pre-processing and manual or semi-automatic region-of-interest (ROI) tracking, limiting their practical applicability. This study proposes a deep learning-based method for estimating f_R directly from thermal videos, eliminating the need for complex pre-processing and ROI tracking. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) is developed to operate on raw thermal video data. To address challenges related to small datasets, the model is trained using data augmentation and transfer learning from synthetic datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a validation R^2 score of approximately 0.61 on both pre-processed and raw thermal videos. By simplifying the workflow, this method holds promise for enhancing the feasibility of thermal imaging in real-world applications, such as remote healthcare and driver monitoring in automotive applications.

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26347
作者: Chi-Wei Lee,An-Kai Chen,Cheng-Han Chiang,Yi-Chun Chang,Po-Chih Kuo

Abstract:For 4D reconstruction, a synchronized multi-camera rig records all views at the same timestamps and misses the motion between them. Staggered triggers spread the same frames over more timestamps. However, when the cameras along each row fire one after another, as in 4DSloMo’s schedule on the N3DV rig, the row acts as one moving camera that confounds depth with motion. We introduce OffBeat, which models a staggered rig as a spatially distributed multicoset sampler: shifted copies of one sampling grid. From the calibration alone, OffBeat derives camera groups that fire together and their firing order. Since one group records each timestamp, a short-lived primitive can fit an error its cameras share, such as a color offset, and flicker in novel views. We show that a primitive’s opacity over time weights all groups equally, for every number of groups, only if it lasts at least one camera frame interval. On Spacetime Gaussians, a minimum lifetime approximates this bound, and a closed-form smoothed box of that length satisfies it exactly, with less flicker than a Gaussian in its place at nearly equal PSNR. In simulated staggered capture on N3DV, OffBeat outperforms the full 4DSloMo pipeline with video diffusion on every test frame, by 3.04 dB in mean dynamic-region PSNR. Between the first and last synchronized frame, it outperforms the best synchronized method of each scene, with or without frame interpolation, by 1.98 dB in mean dynamic-region PSNR, while synchronized capture is better at its own frames. On PanopticSports, in this frame range, OffBeat is comparable in PSNR to synchronized capture with interpolation. On every N3DV scene, replacing 4DSloMo’s schedule with ours raises the dynamic-region PSNR of Spacetime Gaussians, 4DSloMo without diffusion, and our reconstruction. Multi-camera rigs could follow faster motion at the same frame count by changing only when each camera fires.

作者: Ryan Lucas,Petros Prastakos,Rahul Mazumder
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Video diffusion transformers reuse key–value (KV) caches across denoising steps, which quickly becomes a bottleneck for long video generation. We find that quantizing temporally distant cache vectors leads to a large range and high quantization error, but that nearby video tokens in the KV-cache share a persistent pattern per channel. These patterns also vary across videos, motivating rotations that are adapted to each video’s unique cache. We propose Temporal Rotation Quantization (TRQ), a method that rotates frames in the cache that are adjacent in time before quantization. For each block of temporally adjacent cache vectors, TRQ fits an orthogonal transform that maps the block’s per-channel means to a vector that is close to a constant across channels. To keep the quantization format lightweight, we parameterize this rotation as a tree of 2 \times 2 planar rotations, each stored with only two bits, followed by a fixed Hadamard transform shared across all blocks. The rotations are fit without gradients or changes to model weights, and we prove that a simple greedy fit is globally optimal for our ‘mean-flattening’ objective. The transforms are fit online for each new video, and we release fused Triton kernels to make this process efficient at inference. At 2-bit precision and matched compression, TRQ improves VBench subject consistency over the state-of-the-art method QVG from 90.38 to 92.02 on LongCat-Video-13B and from 86.33 to 87.61 on HY-WorldPlay-8B, as well as improving other metrics.

Abstract:Single-photon lidar records the arrival time of each returning photon, enabling 3D reconstruction from few views and scarce photons. However, leading neural methods such as Transientangelo require over an hour of non-convex per-scene optimization, and their accuracy degrades as photon flux decreases. We propose FirstCross, a network-free approach that instead solves a short sequence of convex problems on a voxel grid. For a solid object, the Poisson likelihood of a ray with given signal and background rates depends on the scene solely through its first crossing, the point where the ray first enters the object. Decomposing this likelihood yields two tractable terms. The first penalizes surfaces in front of detected photons and admits a tight convex closure, namely volume rendering with a running-maximum transmittance in place of NeRF’s product transmittance. The second accounts for photons that no surface explains and admits a convex upper bound once the object is assumed to be thick behind each detected surface point. Compared with Transientangelo under its own real-data protocol, FirstCross achieves lower depth error across every test scene, view count, and flux level. With three views and 100 times fewer photons than at the protocol’s lowest flux, our mean object depth error stays under half of Transientangelo’s with all photons. Given our detected surface points, the best classical fusion has 1.3 to 1.8 times our three-view error across flux levels. On real room-scale captures with 1% of their photons, TransientNeRF has 2.8 to 7.7 times our error. FirstCross lets few-view single-photon scanners cut exposure to 1% and reconstruct an object in about a minute on one GPU.

作者: Guojian Zhan,Jiahao Xu,Yahui Liu,Yao Hu,Chuan Mu

Abstract:Agentic visual reasoning improves vision-language models by selectively enlarging evidence without adding new scene content, but the benefit depends on whether fine structure remains accessible and whether local observations stay grounded in the full scene. We identify three recurring bottlenecks: high-frequency detail can be attenuated during visual-token formation; spatially distributed evidence can remain encoded yet difficult for the language model to retrieve; and isolated crops can weaken whole-detail correspondence through scale and positional mismatch. ResVision addresses these limitations with two complementary components. Spectrum-Matched Resizing (SMR) estimates image complexity and selects an adaptive global sampling scale, avoiding unnecessary enlargement on simple inputs while allocating more visual tokens to detail-rich images. Context-Preserving Inspection (CPI) returns each inspected crop together with the complete working view, preserving local detail and global context across tool turns. We evaluate Direct and Agentic variants on four frontier VLMs and 29 benchmarks spanning six visual-reasoning families. Complete ResVision (Agentic Base plus SMR plus CPI) is best for every model, improving by 3.36 to 4.94 points over Direct Base and 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base. These results show that adaptive visual sampling and context-preserving inspection address distinct, complementary constraints in multimodal reasoning.

Abstract:Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. Abstract:Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pretrained source model to unlabeled target domains without source data access, yet two critical failure modes remain unaddressed. Abstract:Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Abstract:Autonomous rendezvous and proximity operations require not only an accurate estimate of the pose of the target spacecraft, but also a reliable indication of when this estimate can be trusted. Abstract:We present PaveSplat, a feed-forward Gaussian splatting method that adds a learned residual to the analytic surface-aligned covariance, keeping surfels paving the visible surface across rendering resolutions. Abstract:Robotic world models predict future video frames from the current observation and a sequence of robot actions. [CV-78] Why Flat Drafts Stay Flat: Region-Mean Latents Govern Texture in Flow-Based Image Generation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25930
作者: Zihan Gu,Jiangcan Jia,Hua Zhang,Lulu Zhao
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Flat color-block drafts specify layout and regional color while leaving interior detail unspecified, yet pretrained flow-based generators can preserve their flat appearance even under photorealistic prompts. We trace this behavior to a cross-scale mechanism linking fine pixel variation to regional means in variational autoencoder (VAE) latent space. Flattening photo regions systematically shifts their latent means, with offsets concentrated along a shared channel direction within each backbone. Controlled field exchanges in FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image establish the effect of this displacement on texture generation: adding the photo-derived regional mean field to a flat latent restores texture, whereas adding its complementary field alone largely preserves flatness. A second-order encoding expansion explains how encoder curvature can convert zero-mean perturbations into mean shifts. An analytically solvable conditional Gaussian flow shows how regional noise averaging enables near-unit endpoint sensitivity at high signal-to-noise ratios. This mechanism motivates training-free rendering through pixel dither before encoding, mean-field scaling, and early boundary holding. Paired low-rank adaptation (LoRA) with draft conditioning improves content recovery and produces photo-like regional means under the standard velocity objective. Explicit regional mean guidance remains effective after adaptation, continuously controlling texture and improving color fidelity. These findings connect encoding shifts to persistent generation behavior and support interventions evaluated for texture, spatial fidelity, and semantic recovery.

[CV-79] SpatialMem: Building Quantitative Spatial Reasoning Agents with Hierarchical Memory

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25925
作者: Zinan Zheng,Nuo Chen,Jia Li
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in qualitative spatial reasoning, but remain limited in quantitative spatial reasoning. Current work leverages the VLM agent to invoke external vision tools to perform computation. However, these methods usually bind each functional requirement to a single predefined vision specialist, implicitly resulting in fixed and rigid tool pipelines. In practice, addressing diverse spatial scenarios and tasks demands a broader diversity in pipeline orchestration and vision specialist selection to achieve robust spatial reasoning. However, such diversity leads to a combinatorial execution space, making it challenging for the agent to orchestrate the optimal pipelines and specialists for different scenarios. In this work, we propose SpatialMem, a memory framework that enables a VLM agent to accumulate tool-use experience and leverage that memory to orchestrate vision specialists to solve the spatial reasoning problem. SpatialMem builds a two-level memory structure, with task memory capturing tool orchestration and scene memory capturing tool selection. It further introduces a dual-state trajectory optimization process to preserve successful tool experiences and refine suboptimal ones. Moreover, existing spatial reasoning benchmarks suffer from quality issues and limited coverage of scene types and tasks. To address these gap, we propose MetricBench, a benchmark covering both indoor and outdoor scenes and three quantitative spatial reasoning tasks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on MetricBench, Q-Spatial, and SpatilRGPT-Bench, outperforming best VLM baselines by 32% on MetricBench. Additionally, the memory design yields a 9.1% absolute gain over a memory-free agent on MetricBench. [CV-80] Multiple-Camera Tracking of Rigid Objects

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25904
作者: Frédérick Martin,Radu Horaud
类目: Robotics (cs.RO); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:In this paper we describe a method for tracking rigid objects using one or several cameras. The tracking process consists of aligning a 3-D model representation of an object with image contours by measuring and minimizing the image error between predicted model points and image contours. The tracker behaves like a visual servo loop where the internal and external camera parameters are updated at each new image acquisition. We study in detail the Jacobian matrix associated with this minimization process in the presence of both point-to-point and point-to-contour matches. We establish the minimal number of matches that are needed as well as the singular configurations leading to a rank-defficient Jacobian matrix. We find a mathematical link between the point-to-point and point-to-contour cases. Based on this link we show that the latter has the same kind of singularities than the former. Moreover, we study multiple camera configurations which optimize the robustness of the method in the presence of single-camera singularities, bad, noisy, or missing data. Extensive experiments done with a complex ship part and with up to three cameras validate the method. In particular we show that the tracker may well be used as a camera calibration procedure.

[CV-81] Does It Depend on the Split? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping

作者: Dharani Deivasihamani,Nandakishore Puttashamachar

Abstract:Self-supervised foundation models are often said to need fewer labels than supervised training. We test this on a forestry task: classifying 20 tree species classes in 0.2 m aerial images from the TreeSatAI dataset. We compare a frozen DINOv3 model pretrained on 493 million satellite images, with only a linear classifier trained on top, against an ImageNet ResNet-50 that is fine-tuned end to end. On the official split, fine-tuning wins clearly (macro F1 0.764 vs. 0.685). However, 28.8% of the official test patches overlap a training or validation patch, and copying the label of the nearest such patch is correct for 83.6% of them. We therefore build a spatial split that holds out whole 2 km squares with a 200 m buffer. On this split the comparison becomes inconclusive (0.648 vs. 0.640, paired 95% CI of the difference [-0.054, 0.016]), and the learning curves of the two models overlap at every label budget from 343 to 33,126 training patches. On the five rarest classes, the frozen model achieves a higher mean F1 (0.566 vs. 0.445), although the confidence interval for this difference includes zero ([-0.05, 0.23]). Diagnostics show that the frozen features mainly miss differences between closely related species, such as the two native oaks. Choosing the input size and layer on validation data (224 px, block 16) raises the frozen model to 0.662 on the spatial split. A comparison that looks decisive on the official split is thus inconclusive under geographically separated evaluation. We release the spatial split and our code.
